name: File system paths and directories
plain: Sites cannot list your folders or see where files live.
meaning: The File System Access API (Chromium) returns handles after a picker; the real path is withheld (fakepath). OPFS is a private sandbox. Only the file name, size and last modified are readable.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: proxy: OPFS
fields.range: private origin sandbox, no host paths

limits.headline: Can't see your folders or where your files are stored
limits.user_action: You tap Choose file or Open file and pick one in the file picker
can: Open the file you pick, once or for the visit
See its name, size, and last changed date
Save back to a file you picked, after you agree in Chrome or Edge
Use a private storage area just for the site
cannot: See the folder path; browsers hide it
List files you did not pick
Open a file or folder without a picker
See your OS folders or home directory
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge let you pick files for later saving. Safari and Firefox only give one time picks.

story.what_it_is: Sites cannot see your folders or where your files live. They only get the file you choose.

marketing.name: File System Access API
marketing.pitch: Chrome describes a way for web apps to open and save files you pick, as if they were desktop apps.

story.for_you: When you pick a file to upload, the site gets the file, not the folder path. The path shows as something like fakepath. Chrome also lets a site save to a file you chose after you approve it.
story.for_makers: Folder paths reveal a person's name and how they organise their life. Web apps need the file itself, not the place. Pickers give that, and the browser keeps the real path hidden.

use_cases.example: A browser photo editor opens the picture you chose and saves back after you approve, without ever seeing your folders.
A web code editor opens a project folder you pick and cannot browse the rest of the disk.
A browser game lets you load a save file you choose and cannot scan for others.
A print shop site uploads the one picture you picked and cannot see other photos.
A malicious page wanted to search for files like wallet or password files, which the web blocks.
A company portal accepts a spreadsheet you pick and cannot explore your drives.
A browser music tool loads your chosen samples and cannot browse your library.

legit_uses: None: the browser deliberately withholds it
abuse: Sites attempt proxies to recover it
